title: From DQ to European Record: Sara Curtis Stuns at Sette Colli Trophy
summary: The 2026 Sette Colli Trophy kicked off with drama before the first splash. Italian sprinter Sara Curtis was disqualified in the prelims of the women's 50 backstroke, only to have the decision overturned on appeal. Given a second chance, the 19-year-old seized it with both hands. In the final, Curtis exploded off the wall and never looked back, touching in 27.07—a new European Record. She erased Dutch swimmer Kira Toussaint's 2021 mark of 27.10 and moved to second in the world rankings this season, behind only American Katharine Berkoff's 26.98. "I was so nervous after this morning," Curtis said poolside. "But the crowd gave me energy." Her performance headlined a night of upsets and breakthroughs. Olympic champion Adam Peaty failed to qualify for the men's 50 breaststroke final, while world record-holder Thomas Ceccon missed the 100 fly 'A' final. Their absences cracked the door for underdogs. In the men's 400 freestyle, Italy's Marco De Tullio dominated from the first 50 meters, splitting 26.32 and building a lead he never surrendered. He finished in 3:45.10, nearly two seconds clear of teammate Alessandro Ragaini. "I just wanted to swim my own race," De Tullio said. The meet also features a marquee clash in the women's 50 butterfly: American Gretchen Walsh versus Swedish legend Sarah Sjöström, their first butterfly duel since the 2023 World Championships. And in the men's 50 backstroke, Greece's Apostolos Christou (25.08) edged Italy's Francesco Lazzari (25.15) by a fingertip. With the Commonwealth Games, Pan Pacs, and European Championships looming, the Sette Colli Trophy is proving a crucial tune-up—and a showcase of rising stars.
why_it_matters: Swimming fans get a preview of rising stars who could dominate future Olympics; unexpected champions and upsets show how competitive the sport is even without the biggest medals on the line.

background_read: The Sette Colli Trophy is an annual international swimming competition held in Rome, drawing many top athletes as a warm-up for major championships.
Kira Toussaint (Dutch swimmer) set the previous European 50 backstroke record of 27.10 in 2021, and Katharine Berkoff (American) currently leads the world rankings with 26.98.

Olympic champion Adam Peaty (Great Britain's most decorated breaststroke swimmer, with three Olympic golds) and world record-holder Thomas Ceccon (Italy's dominant backstroke and butterfly star) are among the biggest names in the sport.

The Commonwealth Games (a multi-sport event for Commonwealth nations), Pan Pacific Championships (for nations bordering the Pacific), and European Championships are all major 2026 meets, so the Sette Colli serves as a crucial tune-up.

perspectives.description: Sara Curtis turned a disqualification into a European Record, showing resilience. Her success, alongside Marco De Tullio's, proves young talent can rise when big names falter.

When Olympic champions like Peaty and Ceccon fail to reach finals, it raises questions about their form before major meets. A tune-up that exposes serious gaps could rattle confidence rather than build it.

perspectives.perspective: Neutral / analytical – the shifting pecking order
perspectives.description: The 2025-2026 season has no Olympics or Worlds, so lower-tier meets become experiments. The results hint at a generational shift in sprint events, with records falling even in a less-pressurized setting.

perspectives.perspective: Forward-looking – what this means for the summer championships
perspectives.description: With European Champs, Pan Pacs, and Commonwealth Games ahead, the Sette Colli shows who is peaking. If Curtis and De Tullio carry this momentum, medal predictions for those meets will need a rewrite.
